evals.name: purchase-split-closing-costs
evals.prompt: I bought a house (call it OakSt, commodity OAKST) on 2026-02-01 for $500,000: $115,000 cash from Assets:Checking and a $400,000 mortgage. Closing costs: $10,000 title/transfer capitalized into basis, $2,000 in fees expensed to Expenses:ClosingCosts, and a $3,000 escrow seed. Record it in ./ledger.beancount.
evals.expected_output: Proposal opens Assets:Property:OakSt (OAKST), Assets:Escrow:OakSt, Liabilities:Mortgage:OakSt and books the purchase: 1 OAKST {510000.00 USD} (500000 price + 10000 capitalized), escrow seed 3000.00, expensed fees 2000.00, cash -115000.00, mortgage -400000.00, with the 515000 = 115000 + 400000 tie-out shown. Nothing written before confirmation; after the yes the check passes and the mortgage balance is -400000.00.
expectations: The property lot's basis is 510000.00 (capitalized costs included) and the 2000.00 fees are a separate expense leg
The closing arithmetic tie-out (515000 both sides) is shown in the proposal
New accounts are proposed as opens, not silently created or assumed

evals.name: mortgage-payment-ties-to-statement
evals.prompt: Record the March mortgage payment for OakSt in ./ledger.beancount, paid 2026-03-01 from Assets:Checking. The statement says: total $2,400.00 — principal $600.00, interest $1,500.00, escrow $300.00, new balance $399,400.00.
evals.expected_output: Both gates shown tied (600+1500+300 = 2400; ledger balance -400000.00 + 600 = statement -399400.00), the four-leg entry proposed in full, nothing written before confirmation; after the yes the mortgage balance reads -399400.00 and escrow 3300.00, check passes.
expectations: Principal is taken from the statement figures given, and the balance tie-out to 399400.00 is shown
The entry has principal +600.00 to the mortgage, interest 1500.00 expensed, escrow +300.00 as an asset

evals.name: payment-without-split-asks
evals.prompt: Record my March mortgage payment for OakSt in ./ledger.beancount: $2,400 paid on 2026-03-01 from checking. The rate is 6% if you need it.
evals.expected_output: No entry is proposed from the rate. The skill asks for the statement's printed principal/interest/escrow breakdown (and new balance), explains it does not amortize or derive the split, and writes nothing.
expectations: The printed split is requested instead of any computed breakdown
No amortization math is presented as the split
Nothing is written to the ledger

evals.name: rent-and-deposit-not-income-twice
evals.prompt: For the OakSt rental in ./ledger.beancount: my tenant paid April rent of $1,800 on 2026-04-05, and back on 2026-03-15 they paid a $1,800 security deposit. Record both into Assets:Checking.
evals.expected_output: Rent booked against a per-property rent income account (Income:Rent:OakSt, its open proposed since it does not exist yet); the deposit booked as a liability (Liabilities:Deposits:OakSt or as proposed), explicitly not income. Both shown in one proposal; nothing written before confirmation.
expectations: Rent goes to a per-property rent income account (open proposed if missing)
The security deposit is a liability while held, not income

evals.name: sale-closes-lot-and-mortgage
evals.prompt: I sold OakSt on 2027-06-01 for $650,000. The closing disclosure: mortgage payoff $399,400, closing costs $10,000 (to Expenses:ClosingCosts), net cash to Assets:Checking, and the $2,100 escrow balance refunded to checking too. Record the sale in ./ledger.beancount.
evals.expected_output: Gates shown: ledger mortgage -399400.00 equals the stated payoff; 650000 = 240600 net cash + 399400 + 10000. Sale entry reduces the 510000.00 lot @ 650000 with the gains leg inferred (booking produces 140000.00), escrow refund as its own transfer. After the yes: property 0 units, mortgage 0, escrow 0, check passes. Accounts are not closed as part of the sale.
expectations: Both gates (payoff equals ledger balance; price arithmetic) are shown before proposing
The gain is booking-produced (140000.00), never typed as a figure
After writing, property/mortgage/escrow balances are zero and accounts remain open
